findings.title: Q1 — The crawling ACTIVE variant @0x80101210 uses DIFFERENT decision/executor tables (0x8010C90C / 0x8010C918), not the upright ones
findings.meaning: Structurally identical to the upright variant (same two-phase decision-then-executor call on the same sub_state_1 = entity+0x5), but it indexes two SEPARATE tables. lui at,0x8011 = 0x80110000; 0x80110000-14196 = 0x8010C88C (upright decision), -14132 = 0x8010C8CC (upright executor), -14068 = 0x8010C90C (CRAWL decision), -14056 = 0x8010C918 (CRAWL executor). Port note: the delay slots `addu s2,a2,zero` (0x8010124C) and `addu a2,s2,zero` (0x80101274) execute BEFORE the jalr, i.e. a2 is stashed in s2 before the decision call and restored as the 3rd argument to the executor. Neither variant masks entity+0x5 before indexing.

verdict.why:
CORE CLAIM CONFIRMED, but the interpretation is incomplete in a load-bearing way and one MIPS statement is worded backwards.

== WHAT I INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED (PROVEN) ==
My own `re2_disasm.py dis 0x8010118c 40 --bin EMZ0.BIN` and `dis 0x80101210 40` return instruction-for-instruction exactly what the claim quoted, including every nop. No fabrication.

Raw encodings confirm all four constants at the quoted addresses (`bytes` output):
  80101240: 0c c9 22 8c   -> lw v0, 0xC90C(at)
  80101268: 18 c9 22 8c   -> lw v0, 0xC918(at)
  801011bc: 8c c8 22 8c   -> lw v0, 0xC88C(at)
  801011e4: cc c8 22 8c   -> lw v0, 0xC8CC(at)
With `lui at,0x8011` (at=0x80110000) the negative immediates are literally the low halfword of the target: 0x8010C88C / 0x8010C8CC (upright) and 0x8010C90C / 0x8010C918 (crawl). So "different tables" is PROVEN.

DELAY SLOT ASSIGNMENT (checked): correct. `8010124c: addu s2,a2,zero` is the delay slot of `80101248: jalr v0`; `80101274: addu a2,s2,zero` is the delay slot of `80101270: jalr v0`. Same shape in the upright variant at 0x801011c8 / 0x801011f0. Nothing is inverted.

NO MASK (checked): `8010122c: lbu v0,5(s0)` / `80101230: nop` / `80101234: sll v0,v0,2` — no andi. Same upright at 0x801011a8/0x801011b0. Claim correct.

== DEFECT 1 — "structurally identical" hides that the CRAWL tables are 3 entries, not 16 ==
`table 0x8010C90C 16` shows the pointer run dies after 3 entries:
  [0] 0x8010c90c -> 0x80102ee4
  [1] 0x8010c910 -> 0x801025e4
  [2] 0x8010c914 -> 0x80103a70
  [3] 0x8010c918 -> 0x80103024   <-- this IS the executor table
  [6] 0x8010c924 -> 0x803200be   <-- not a pointer
Raw bytes 0x8010c90c: `e4 2e 10 80 e4 25 10 80 70 3a 10 80 | 24 30 10 80 ec 25 10 80 48 3b 10 80 | be 00 32 80 ...`

The 0x8010C924 boundary is HARD-PROVEN, not inferred: it is read as HALFWORD data by the already-ported WALK executor:
  80101bc0: lb   v0,363(s1)        (+0x16B gait row)
  80101bc8: sll  v0,v0,1           (halfword stride)
  80101bd4: lhu  v0,-14044(at)     0x8010c924
plus the same lhu at 0x80101ab4 and 0x80101b7c. So the crawl EXECUTOR table is bounded to exactly 0x8010C918/C91C/C920 (3 entries), and the crawl DECISION table to 0x8010C90C/C910/C914 (3 entries).

A whole-overlay disassembly scan (0x80100000..0x8010C830) finds exactly FIVE readers of this region — 0x8010c854 @0x8010116c, 0x8010c88c @0x801011bc, 0x8010c8cc @0x801011e4, 0x8010c90c @0x80101240, 0x8010c918 @0x80101268 — and nothing that would imply larger crawl tables.

Why this matters for the port: the claim's own "Neither variant masks entity+0x5 before indexing" combined with 3-entry tables means crawl sub_state_1 >= 3 falls straight into the executor table, and >= 6 into the gait halfword data (jumping to 0x803200be). Anyone reading "structurally identical" next to the ESTABLISHED "16 entries each" will allocate 16-entry crawl tables and port garbage.

== DEFECT 2 — delay-slot wording is backwards ==
The claim writes: "the delay slots `addu s2,a2,zero` (0x8010124C) and `addu a2,s2,zero` (0x80101274) execute BEFORE the jalr". In MIPS the delay slot is the instruction AFTER the jump and executes AFTER it, before control reaches the target. The instructions were assigned to the right jalrs and the functional consequence stated is right, so this is wording, not a logic inversion — but on a task where delay-slot ordering is the stated failure mode it must not stand.

== NOT THE CLAIM'S BURDEN, VERIFIED ANYWAY ==
`8010114c: addiu sp,sp,-24 / 80101154: lhu v0,270(a0) / 8010115c: andi v0,v0,0x3f / 80101160: sll v0,v0,2 / 8010116c: lw v0,-14252(at) 0x8010c854 / 80101174: jalr v0 / 80101178: nop` (delay slot is a nop — no arg setup). `table 0x8010C854` alternates 0x8010118c / 0x80101210 for 14 entries (C854..C88B, bounded by the upright decision table at 0x8010C88C), so the variant is chosen by the LSB of (+0x10E & 0x3F). INFERRED, not proven: with andi 0x3f allowing 0..63, selectors >= 14 index the decision/executor tables as function pointers — I did not find a writer that bounds +0x10E, so that is UNKNOWN.

Callee sanity (PROVEN): crawl decision[0] 0x80102ee4 and [2] 0x80103a70 and executor[0] 0x80103024 all start with `addiu sp,sp,-32`; executor[2] 0x80103b48 is a leaf starting `lbu v0,6(a0)`. crawl[1] decision 0x801025e4 is `jr ra / nop` — a NO-OP stub, and it is the SAME pointer as upright decision[3]; likewise crawl executor[1] 0x801025ec == upright executor[3]. So the two table sets are separate but partially share handlers.

findings.meaning: The upright decision table occupies 0x8010C88C..0x8010C8CB (16 entries) and the upright executor 0x8010C8CC..0x8010C90B (16 entries). The crawl decision table starts immediately after at 0x8010C90C and is only 3 words long, because 0x8010C918 (= +12) is the crawl executor table, which is likewise 3 words long because 0x8010C924 is the already-ported gait data table. So a crawling zombie has a valid sub_state_1 domain of {0,1,2} ONLY — there is no bounds check in 0x80101210, so any other value reads past the table. Crawl entry [1] resolves to 0x801025e4/0x801025ec which is byte-identical to upright entry [3] (decision is a bare `jr ra` stub, all the work is in the executor). Crawl executor[0] sets motion word entity+0x14C = 0x000F0005 and advances entity+0x6 to 1; crawl executor[2] sets entity+0x14C = 23 (0x17) once and latches entity+0x6 = 1.
openQuestions: What guarantees sub_state_1 stays in {0,1,2} while crawling? The two crawl-entry paths I proved (Finding 7/8) both write 0, 1 or 2, but I have not exhaustively audited every writer of entity+0x5 for the crawl case.

verdict.why:
I could not break it. Every quoted instruction, address and constant reproduces byte-exact, all delay slots are assigned correctly, and the two load-bearing structural bounds are PROVEN rather than assumed.

1) TABLE CONTENTS — verified with `bytes` (raw), not just the decoded `table` view:
  8010c90c: e4 2e 10 80  e4 25 10 80  70 3a 10 80  24 30 10 80
  8010c91c: ec 25 10 80  48 3b 10 80  be 00 32 80  96 00 40 80
Matches the claim's [32]..[38] exactly.

2) THREE DECISION ENTRIES = PROVEN, not inferred from adjacency. The crawl dispatcher itself carries both bases 12 bytes apart:
  80101234: sll v0,v0,2
  80101240: lw v0,-14068(at)    -> 0x8010c90c   (decision base)
  80101268: lw v0,-14056(at)    -> 0x8010c918   (executor base)
0x8010c918 - 0x8010c90c = 12 = 3 words. The claim is right that the decision table cannot be longer.

3) THREE EXECUTOR ENTRIES = PROVEN. 0x8010c924 is read as HALFWORD data, so it cannot be a pointer slot:
  80101ab4: lhu v1,-14044(at)   -> 0x8010c924
  80101abc: andi v1,v1,0x7fff
Raw bytes there are `be 00 32 80` = 0x00be / 0x8032, and 0x8032 & 0x7fff = 0x0032 — a halfword pair, exactly as the gait-table reader consumes it. 0x803200be is not a valid code address in this overlay either.

4) NO BOUNDS CHECK — confirmed. Between 0x8010122c `lbu v0,5(s0)` and 0x80101248 `jalr v0` there is only `sll v0,v0,2` / `lui at,0x8011` / `addu at,at,v0` / `lw`. Same for the second dispatch at 0x80101254..0x80101270. No slt/slti/andi clamp.

5) SHARED HANDLER — confirmed from the raw table: crawl decision[1] @0x8010c910 = 0x801025e4 and crawl executor[1] @0x8010c91c = 0x801025ec are the SAME addresses as upright decision[3] @0x8010c898 = 0x801025e4 and upright executor[3] @0x8010c8d8 = 0x801025ec. And 0x801025e4 really is a standalone 2-instruction stub, not a mis-read function tail — the preceding function ends at 0x801025dc `jr ra` / 0x801025e0 `nop`, then 0x801025e4 `jr ra` / 0x801025e8 `nop`, then 0x801025ec `addiu sp,sp,-104`.

6) DELAY SLOTS re-checked, the claim's readings survive:
  80103b50: bne v0,zero,0x80103b64
  80103b54: addiu v0,zero,1        <- delay slot, only LOADS v0
  80103b58: sb v0,6(a0)            <- past branch target check
  80103b5c: addiu v0,zero,23
  80103b60: sw v0,332(a0)
so "+0x14C=23 once, latch +0x6=1" is correct (the always-executed delay slot has no side effect on memory).
  80103070: addiu v0,zero,1
  80103074: jal 0x80015fe8
  80103078: sb v0,6(s0)            <- delay slot, +0x6=1 committed before the call
correct as claimed.

7) CONSTANTS verified at the quoted addresses: 80103064 `lui v0,0xf` + 80103068 `ori v0,v0,0x5` = 0x000F0005, stored `sw v0,332(s0)` (332 = 0x14C); 80103b5c `addiu v0,zero,23` stored `sw v0,332(a0)`.

8) INDEPENDENT SUPPORT the claim did not have: all three crawl decision functions write the identical state word 257 = 0x00000101 (+0x4=1 ACTIVE, +0x5=1, +0x6=0), each in a bne delay slot followed by the store:
  80102fa4 addiu v0,zero,257 / 80102fa8 sw v0,4(s1)
  80102ff0 addiu v0,zero,257 / 80102ff4 sw v0,4(s1)
  80103b14 sw v0,4(s0)  (v0=257 from delay slot 80103b10)
So crawl sub 0 and crawl sub 2 both route into the shared sub 1 — consistent with, and supporting, a {0,1,2} domain.
verdict.correction:
Claim stands; two labels in "ITS MEANING" are INFERRED rather than PROVEN and should be marked as such before porting.

(a) "motion word entity+0x14C" — the claim cites no reader. I found readers, and they support the label but show the format is NOT uniform. The read-modify-write pattern appears twice:
  80101a7c: lbu v0,536(s1)      (+0x218 = desired id)
  80101a80: lui v1,0xf
  80101a84: addu v0,v0,v1
  80101a8c: sw v0,332(s1)       (delay slot of jal 0x80015fe8)
and
  801054bc: lbu v1,536(s1)
  801054c0: lbu v0,332(s1)      (current id = LOW BYTE of the word)
  801054c8: beq v1,v0,0x801054d8
  801054cc: lui v0,0xf          (delay slot)
  801054d0: addu v0,v1,v0
  801054d4: sw v0,332(s1)
i.e. +0x14C is written as a word whose high half is 0x000F and whose LOW BYTE is the id that gets compared back. But crawl executor[2] writes 23 = 0x00000017 — high half 0x0000, not 0x000F. So "+0x14C = motion word" is a reasonable label but the two crawl values are not the same encoding, and the actual consumer is outside this overlay (88 word-stores to 332 in EMZ0, only byte-loads back). Port the raw word stores; do not port a decomposed "motion id / flags" struct until the EXE-side reader is found.

(b) "a crawling zombie has a valid sub_state_1 domain of {0,1,2} ONLY" — this is proven about the TABLE EXTENT, not about the runtime value. Crawl-vs-upright is selected by a different field entirely:
  80101154: lhu v0,270(a0)      (+0x10E)
  8010115c: andi v0,v0,0x3f
  8010116c: lw v0,-14252(at)    -> 0x8010c854
so nothing structurally prevents an entity from being switched to the crawl variant while +0x5 still holds a value >= 3 left over from upright logic; the claim's own "no bounds check ... reads past the table" is the honest form. Note the same overlay demonstrably does index tables with a mask wider than the table: the variant table @0x8010c854 is only 14 entries (it is bounded by the upright decision table at 0x8010c88c, entries [0..13] alternating 0x8010118c/0x80101210) yet the index is masked with 0x3F (0..63). So out-of-range indexing is architecturally normal here and must not be "fixed" with an invented clamp in the port.

findings.title: Q2 — +0x10E is a u16 whose LOW 6 BITS select upright vs crawling through the 14-entry table @0x8010C854 (odd index = crawl)
findings.meaning: +0x10E is loaded as a HALFWORD (lhu, not lbu) and masked with 0x3F, so the variant selector is a 6-bit field; the upper 10 bits (0x0400, 0x2000, 0x4000, 0x8000 all seen in use) are independent flags carried in the same halfword. The table has exactly 14 entries — it butts against the decision table at 0x8010C88C — and strictly alternates upright/crawl, so bit 0 of the 6-bit field IS the crawl selector, and the remaining bits 1..5 are a spawn-pose sub-variant that INIT decodes. This must be ported as a 14-entry table, not as an `if (variant & 1)`, because a variant >= 14 would run off the end into the decision table.

verdict.why:
REFUTED — the instruction block is real and correctly transcribed, but the MEANING contains two INVENTED flag bits (misattributed from neighbouring instructions on OTHER fields), a refuted "INIT-only" characterization, and a port prescription that contradicts its own stated hazard. Status "PROVEN" is not warranted.

=== FAILURE 1 (fatal): 0x0400 and 0x8000 are NOT bits of +0x10E ===

  andi 0x0001 x9 | andi 0x003f x11 | andi 0x0040 x1 | andi 0x0080 x26
  andi 0x4000 x3 | andi 0xbfff x1 | andi 0xdfff x2 | andi 0xffc0 x1
  ori 0x0001 x1 | ori 0x0080 x1  | ori 0x2000 x5  | ori 0x4000 x3
0x0400 never appears. 0x8000 never appears.
The 0x8000 the claimant saw is on a DIFFERENT field:
  80101cec: lhu v0,538(s1)          ; +0x21A, not +0x10E
  80101cf0: nop
  80101cf4: andi v0,v0,0x8000
and
  801083a8: ori v0,v0,0x8000
  801083ac: sw v0,1376(v1)          ; 32-bit field on another struct
The 0x0400 the claimant saw is a 32-bit constant on the +0x0 flag word:
  80100b38: lui v0,0x400            ; = 0x04000000, not 0x0400

findings.title: Q2c — INIT @0x8010065C decodes the 6-bit variant: it REMAPS 5->2 and 7->4, then does crawl-specific setup when bit0 survives
findings.meaning: INIT is a straight-line chain of `variant == N` tests, NOT a switch. Order matters and it is self-modifying: variant 5 rewrites +0x10E to 0x4002 (variant 2) at 0x80100A38 and variant 7 rewrites it to 0x4004 (variant 4) at 0x80100A8C — both ODD (crawl-indexed) spawn values are converted to EVEN (upright) before the bit0 test at 0x80100AE8 runs, and both additionally set +0x156 = -1 and OR 0x4000 into *(entity+0x198 + 1376). So variants 5 and 7 are 'spawn as X but start upright'. The generic crawl setup (variant bit0 still set at 0x80100AE8) installs a symmetric 200-unit hitbox (+0x90,+0x92,+0x9A,+0x9C = 200; +0x98 = -350, +0x9E = +350), sets motion +0x14C = 23, ORs 0x2000 into +0x10E, rewrites entity flags +0x0 as (flags & 0xF3FFFFFF) | 0x04000000, and HALVES +0x156 with a round-toward-zero shift (`sra 16 / srl 31 / addu / sra 1`). Watch the delay slots: 0x801009D4 `sw a1,332(s2)` and 0x80100AB8 `addiu v0,zero,257` and 0x80100B70 `addiu v0,zero,513` all execute unconditionally.
openQuestions: The semantics of the individual non-crawl spawn variants (2,3,4,6,8,10, ...) — I decoded their state/motion writes but not what pose each represents.
*(entity+0x198 + 1376) |= 0x4000 — the +0x198 struct is the model/animation instance; the meaning of bit 0x4000 at +0x560 of it is unresolved.

verdict.why:
The instruction transcription is byte-accurate and two core assertions independently check out (5->0x4002 @0x80100A34/A38 bytes `02 40 02 24`/`0e 01 42 a6`, 7->0x4004 @0x80100A88/A8C bytes `04 40 02 24`; and odd=crawl is PROVEN by table 0x8010C854 which I dumped: idx0..13 alternate 8c 11 10 80 / 10 12 10 80 = 0x8010118C upright / 0x80101210 crawl). The bit0 gate polarity @0x80100AEC and the signed /2 idiom @0x80100B48-B58 are also correct. But three parts of the stated MEANING fail, so it cannot stand as PROVEN.

(1) WRONG MEMORY ACCESS. Claim says "OR 0x4000 into *(entity+0x198 + 1376)", which denotes entity+0x730. The code is a DOUBLE dereference: `80100a48: lw v1,408(s2)` (bytes `98 01 43 8e`) loads a POINTER from entity+0x198, then `80100a54: lw v0,1376(v1)` (`60 05 62 8c`) / `80100a60: sw v0,1376(v1)` (`60 05 62 ac`). That +0x198 is a pointer is independently proven at 0x80100818 `lw v1,408(s2)` -> 0x8010083c `sh v0,1532(v1)` / 0x80100848 `sh v0,1536(v1)`. A port following the claim's expression writes the wrong address.

(2) "installs a symmetric 200-unit hitbox" is wrong twice. It does not INSTALL: the SAME six offsets are already written by the generic path the claim never mentions -- 0x80100958 `addiu v0,zero,-1500` / 0x8010095c `sh v0,152(s2)`; 0x80100960 `addiu v0,zero,1500` / 0x80100964 `sh v0,158(s2)`; 0x8010096c `addiu v1,zero,500` -> `sh v1` to 154,156,144,146; plus 0x80100980 `sh v1,478(s2)` (+0x1EE=500, which crawl NEVER overrides) and 0x80100990/0x80100994 `sh zero,148/150` (+0x94/+0x96=0). So the crawl block is an OVERRIDE, and a port built from the claim alone leaves every even/upright variant with no extents. And it is not "symmetric 200": the grower at 0x80103628-0x80103694 proves two distinct field groups with distinct limits -- `sltiu v0,v1,0x1f4` @0x80103630/0x80103650 caps +0x9A/+0x9C/+0x90/+0x92 at 500, while `slti v0,v0,-1499` @0x80103678 floors +0x98 at -1500 with +0x9E rising. The claim also cited no reader at all for these offsets, so "hitbox" was an uncited interpretation.

(3) `a1` LEFT UNRESOLVED although three of its own quoted instructions depend on it -- and it is set in a DELAY SLOT the claim did not check: `801009b4: bne v1,v0,0x801009c4` (bytes `03 00 62 14`, target = fallthrough+2) with delay slot `801009b8: addiu a1,zero,1` (bytes `01 00 05 24`), so a1 = 1 on BOTH paths. Hence 0x801009D4 `sw a1,332(s2)` = +0x14C = 1 (default motion), 0x80100B6C `bne v0,a1,0x80100b78` is the variant==1 test, and 0x80100B8C `sw a1,4(s2)` = +0x4 = 1 for variant 3. The claim's narrative enumerates the chain as tests for 2,4,5,7,6,8 + bit0 and never states that variants 1 and 3 -- the ONLY crawl variants that survive the remap -- have their own tests at 0x80100B60/0x80100B78 after the crawl block. For a claim whose thesis is which variants stay crawl, that is a hole. (Not the earlier a1=0x80100004 from 0x80100684/0x80100688, which is only the LWL/LWR source pointer for the sp+0x20 copy at 0x8010068C-0x801006A8.)

findings.title: Q4a — Crawling IS reachable from a live standing zombie: HURT executor phase 2 converts it unconditionally
findings.meaning: This answers Q4 decisively: crawling is NOT spawn-only. A zombie taking this hurt/knockdown path runs phase 0 -> 1 -> 2 (phase 1 advances by the return value of the animation stepper 0x8002959C, so phase 2 arrives when the clip ends), and phase 2 writes +0x10E = 0x2001 at 0x80106B10 — 6-bit variant = 1 = CRAWL, plus the same 0x2000 flag INIT sets. It installs the identical crawl hitbox (200/200/200/200, -350/+350) that INIT's crawl branch does, applies the identical flag rewrite (flags & 0xF3FFFFFF) | 0x04000000, sets motion +0x14C = t0 = 0x000F0005 (the motion crawl-executor[0] phase 0 also sets), and sets the state word to t2 = 1 (state 1 ACTIVE, sub_state_1 = 0, sub_state_2 = 0) — i.e. crawl decision[0] 0x80102EE4 / crawl executor[0] 0x80103024. Note t2 was loaded as 1 way back at 0x8010673C and t0/t1 at 0x80106AF0-0x80106AEC, before the branch. Gate: entity+0x231 must be neither 1 nor 2 (0x80106740 / 0x8010675C).
openQuestions: What entity+0x231 is (it selects between 0x80109610, 0x801067B4 and this phase machine) — unresolved.

Which damage/hit conditions route the zombie into the function at 0x801066FC in the first place (i.e. which HURT sub_state_1 it is) — I proved the conversion exists and how phase 2 is reached, not the full entry condition.

verdict.why:
REFUTED ON FRAMING, NOT ON BYTES. I re-disassembled every cited address from EMZ0.BIN; all instructions, all delay slots and all constants in the submission are byte-exact, and I independently confirmed most of the interpretation (details in `correction`). But the STATUS "PROVEN" fails on two counts, both of which would silently corrupt a byte-true port.

FAILURE 1 — "A zombie taking this hurt/knockdown path runs phase 0 -> 1 -> 2" is CONTRADICTED. The claim's listing jumps straight from the phase dispatch (0x80106794) to phase 1 (0x801069b4); it never shows how +0x6 becomes 1, and never shows that phase 0 (0x8010679c) has FOUR escape hatches that latch +0x231 and permanently divert, so phase 1/2 are never reached:
  801067a8: bgez v0,0x801067cc      ; delay 801067ac: addiu v0,zero,2
  801067b0: sb v0,561(s2)           ; DAT 0x800cfbf8 < 0 -> +0x231 = 2 -> jal 0x801092c4 @801067bc, return
  801067cc: lh v0,268(s2)
  801067d4: bne v0,zero,0x8010681c  ; delay 801067d8: addiu v0,zero,1   ; +0x10C != 0 -> +0x231 = 1
  801067e0: lw v0,-1064(v0)         ; 0x800cfbd8
  801067e4: lui v1,0x1000
  801067ec: bne v0,zero,0x8010681c  ; delay 801067f0: addiu v0,zero,1   ; flag 0x10000000 -> +0x231 = 1
  8010681c: sb v0,561(s2)           ; then jal 0x80109610 @80106828, return
Because +0x231 is a stored byte, the gate the claim DID quote (0x80106740 bne v0,t2 / 0x8010675c beq v0,a0) then routes this entity away forever. "Converts it unconditionally" is true only of the phase-2 BLOCK (0x80106a8c-0x80106b58 is straight-line apart from 0x80106adc), not of the conversion.

The claim also omits the instruction that makes the whole thing enemy-state-dependent:
  801067f4: jal 0x80015fe8          ; PRNG
  801067fc: andi v0,v0,0x3
  80106800: beq v0,zero,0x80106838  ; delay 80106804: addiu v0,zero,3
  80106808: lbu v1,4(s2)
  80106810: bne v1,v0,0x8010683c    ; delay 80106814: lui a2,0x3
i.e. if state (+0x4) == 3 the zombie only proceeds 1-in-4; if state != 3 it always proceeds. The actual 0->1 advance the claim never quotes is:
  80106848: addiu v0,zero,1
  8010684c: sb v0,6(s2)             ; +0x6 = 1
Dropping this loses both the 1-in-4 death-crawl roll and the four gates.

FAILURE 2 — "HURT executor", "HURT-side" is ASSERTED, never shown, and is incomplete. The submission contains zero instructions linking the HURT root to 0x801066fc. There is no `jal 0x801066fc` anywhere in EMZ0.BIN; it is reached only through three table slots (0x8010ca40, 0x8010ca64, 0x8010cd24), and 0x8010cd24 belongs to the DEATH root's table, not HURT. Labelling it "the HURT executor" hides the shared use that the unexplained `lbu v1,4(s2)` / `bne v1,v0(=3)` gate exists for.

FAILURE 3 (open, neither of us proved it) — that a caller ever supplies a hit descriptor producing +0x5 == 7 or 8 together with +0x1D2 == 1. The damage routine is called indirectly (no `jal 0x800470c8` exists), so concrete reachability of that exact table cell is structural inference. UNKNOWN, needs a live hit trace or the indirect-call site.

0x801066fc sits at 0x8010ca40 (row 7, col 1) and 0x8010ca64 (row 8, col 1). The DEATH root 0x80108250 uses the identical geometry with base 0x8010cc24 (801084e8/801084ec) and reaches 0x801066fc at 0x8010cd24 (row 7, col 1).

+0x4 IS the state word, and the EXE sets it from HP, which is what the 0x80106810 `bne v1,3` gate keys on:
   8004727c: lh v1,342(s1)               ; HP
   80047284: bgez v1,0x80047294
   80047288: sw v0,4(s1)   (delay, v0=2) ; alive -> state 2 HURT
   8004728c: addiu v0,zero,3 / 80047290: sw v0,4(s1)  ; HP<0 -> state 3 DEATH
So from the HURT table (+0x4 == 2) the phase-0 PRNG roll never applies and phase 1 always follows; from the DEATH table (+0x4 == 3) it is 1-in-4. The word store also zeroes +0x5/+0x6/+0x7, which is why phase starts at 0; +0x5 is then set separately:
   80047324: sb s5,5(s1)                 ; +0x5 = low byte of the hit descriptor (a3, saved at 800470e8)
   80047294: addiu v0,zero,1 / 80047298: sb v0,466(s1)      ; +0x1D2 default 1
   800472d4: sb zero,466(s1)             ; override 0
   80047308: addiu v0,zero,2 / 8004730c: sb v0,466(s1)      ; override 2
   80047318: lbu v0,466(s1) / 80047320: addu v1,v1,s6 / 80047328: addu v0,v0,v1 / 80047330: sb v0,466(s1)
   -> +0x1D2 = (0|1|2) + 3*s6, with s6 = a3 >> 28 (80047114: srl s6,s5,28)
So col 1 requires the default base 1 AND s6 == 0. Legal +0x5 range is 1..18 (the crawler table 0x8010cbe8 has non-null entries [1]..[18], [0] NULL), so rows 7/8 are in range — but I could NOT prove any caller actually emits (a3 & 0xFF) in {7,8} with (a3 >> 28) == 0, because 0x800470c8 is only ever called indirectly. Mark that leg UNKNOWN.

CORRECTED CLAIM: "0x801066fc is a hurt/death knockdown handler shared by the HURT table (0x8010c940 rows 7,8 col 1) and the DEATH table (0x8010cc24 row 7 col 1), reached only for a zombie that was UPRIGHT (+0x10E & 1 == 0). Its phase 2 (+0x6 == 2, 0x80106a8c) is a straight-line conversion to the crawl variant (+0x10E = 0x2001, crawl hitbox and flag rewrite byte-identical to INIT's crawl branch, motion +0x14C = 0x000F0005, state word = 1). Reaching phase 2 is NOT unconditional: phase 0 has four latching exits via +0x231, and for a dying zombie (+0x4 == 3) it additionally requires (PRNG & 3) == 0."

findings.title: Q4b — Second runtime path: the knockdown fork picks CRAWLER vs CORPSE on a global one-crawler latch, then randomizes sub_state_1 to 0 or 2
findings.meaning: This is the byte-true 'does the downed zombie get up as a crawler or stay a corpse' fork, in the function starting 0x80107438. Three conditions must ALL hold to become a crawler: entity+0x16B (the gait row, signed byte) == 0, entity+0x10C == 0, and the global word @0x800CFBD8 must have bit 0x10000000 CLEAR. Otherwise the state word is set to 7 = CORPSE (0x8010A440). Delay-slot care: 0x801077AC `addiu v0,zero,10` runs on both paths but the `sh v0,342(s2)` at 0x801077B0 only on the fall-through; 0x801077D8 `lui a0,0xf3ff` and 0x80107844 `addiu v0,zero,1` likewise always execute. The crawler branch installs the same 200/-350/+350 hitbox, sets +0x10E = 0x2001 (crawl variant 1 + 0x2000), rewrites flags (flags & 0xF3FFFFFF) | 0x04000000, then calls the PRNG 0x80015FE8 and picks the state word from its low bit: rand&1 != 0 -> 1 (sub_state_1 = 0), rand&1 == 0 -> 513 = 0x0201 (sub_state_1 = 2). That the two outcomes are exactly indices 0 and 2 independently confirms Finding Q1b that the crawl tables only have 3 entries.

verdict.why:
REFUTED. Every instruction the claim quotes is byte-accurate, and its three explicit delay-slot notes are correct — but the claim's listing STARTS at 0x801077A0, which amputates the two branches that actually gate the fork. The stated core meaning ("Three conditions must ALL hold to become a crawler: +0x16B==0, +0x10C==0, and bit 0x10000000 of 0x800CFBD8 clear") is FALSE.

=== FATAL #1: +0x16B == 0 is NOT a required condition (a PRNG branch jumps over it) ===
The instruction immediately before the claim's first quoted line:
  8010778c: jal 0x80015fe8
  80107790: nop
  80107794: andi v0,v0,0x3
  80107798: bne v0,zero,0x801077b0        <-- bytes at 0x80107798: 05 00 40 14 = 0x14400005
  8010779c: addiu v0,zero,10              (delay slot)
  801077a0: lb v0,363(s2)                 <-- claim's first line
Target check: 0x14400005 -> 0x8010779C + (5*4) = 0x801077B0. The branch lands ON `sh v0,342(s2)`, i.e. it SKIPS the `lb v0,363(s2)` / `bne v0,zero,0x801077dc` pair entirely. So when (rand & 3) != 0 — three times out of four — entity+0x16B is never read, and a zombie with +0x16B == 1 still becomes a crawler. The claim's "must ALL hold" is contradicted by 0x80107798.

=== FATAL #2: the entity+4 == 3 gate is missing, and it hides a live delay slot ===
  80107470: lbu v1,6(s2)
  ...
  8010749c: addiu v0,zero,2
  801074a0: beq v1,v0,0x8010777c          bytes b6 00 62 10 = 0x106200B6 -> 0x801074A4 + 0x2D8 = 0x8010777C
  801074a4: addiu v0,zero,3               (delay slot -- v0 = 3 is LIVE INTO the fork)
  8010777c: lbu v1,4(s2)
  80107780: nop
  80107784: bne v1,v0,0x801077b4          <-- if entity+4 != 3, jump straight to the +0x10C test
  80107788: nop
This is exactly the delay-slot trap the task warns about: `addiu v0,zero,3` at 0x801074A4 looks dead but is the comparand at 0x80107784. When entity+4 != 3, BOTH the PRNG call and the +0x16B test are bypassed. The claim never mentions this gate.

=== FATAL #3: the claim reports one PRNG call; there are two ===
The claim lists "PRNG 0x80015FE8 @0x80107834" in its constants. There is a second, earlier and more consequential call at `8010778c: jal 0x80015fe8` whose result (`andi v0,v0,0x3`) decides whether the gait byte is consulted at all. Omitting it makes the fork look deterministic where it is not.

=== FATAL #4: "global one-crawler latch" is invented ===
Nothing sets that bit anywhere the claim could cite. Scanning EMZ0.BIN, 0x800CFBD8 is ONLY ever loaded — four sites, zero stores: 0x801002E4, 0x801067E0, 0x801077C8, 0x80108964 (all four then `lui v1,0x1000` / `and` / branch, i.e. all test bit 0x10000000). In PSX.EXE the same word has 80+ accesses across the whole engine (0x80018FE4 ... 0x80077D04), and none of the located stores manipulate bit 0x10000000 with an immediate — e.g. 0x800264B8 `andi v0,v1,0x10` / `ori v0,v1,0x8000`, 0x80035FBC `addiu v1,zero,-8193` / `and`, 0x80052204 `ori v1,v1,0x40`; the rest use runtime register masks (0x8002BA68 `or v1,v1,v0`, 0x80058DF0 `or v0,v0,v1`, 0x80069F90 `or v0,v0,v1`). There is no counter, no set-on-crawler-spawn, nothing "one"-anything. The writer of bit 0x10000000 is UNKNOWN.

=== Weaker but real problems ===
- "+0x16B (the gait row, signed byte)": in THIS function +0x16B is overwritten with a coin flip during phase 0 —
    8010751c: andi v0,v0,0x1
    80107520: beq v0,zero,0x80107680
    80107524: sb v0,363(s2)          (delay slot -- always executes, v0 = rand()&1)
  so at the fork +0x16B is 0 or 1, a fall-direction flag set by this same death sequence. Importing the WALK-executor "gait row" meaning is an unproven reinterpretation.
- "That the two outcomes are exactly indices 0 and 2 independently confirms Finding Q1b that the crawl tables only have 3 entries" — non-sequitur. Outcomes {0,2} are consistent with any table of >= 3 entries; they prove nothing about the upper bound.
- "the function starting 0x80107438" is real (prologue `addiu sp,sp,-64`), but it is one of ~26 stride-12 table entries (0x8010CA3C, 0x8010CA48, ... 0x8010CEA0 all contain 0x80107438), i.e. one death-variant handler, not "the" fork.

=== What DID survive verification (all byte-checked) ===
Instruction text 0x801077A0-0x80107860 matches the tool output exactly. Branch encodings verified from raw bytes: 0x801077A8 `0c 00 40 14` -> 0x801077DC; 0x801077BC `07 00 40 14` -> 0x801077DC; 0x801077D4 `07 00 40 10` -> 0x801077F4; 0x80107840 `02 00 40 14` -> 0x8010784C with delay slot `01 00 02 24` (addiu v0,zero,1) and fallthrough `01 02 02 24` (addiu v0,zero,513). The claim's three delay-slot calls (0x801077AC, 0x801077D8, 0x80107844 all always execute) are CORRECT. Global resolves correctly: `lui v0,0x800d` / `lw v0,-1064(v0)` = 0x800D0000-0x428 = 0x800CFBD8, mask `lui v1,0x1000` = 0x10000000. Constants correct: +0x10E=0x2001 (addiu v1,zero,8193 @0x80107820, sh v1,270(s2) @0x80107824), hitbox 200 @0x801077F8 into +0x9A/+0x9C/+0x90/+0x92, -350 @0x8010780C into +0x98, +350 @0x80107814 into +0x9E, flags (flags & 0xF3FFFFFF)|0x04000000 via `lui a0,0xf3ff`/`ori a0,a0,0xffff`/`lui v1,0x400`, CORPSE state word 7 @0x801077E0. The rand&1 -> 1 vs 513 selection is CORRECT. So the constant table is usable; the control-flow narrative is not.
verdict.correction:
The fork is entered only for entity+6 == 2 (0x801074A0, with v0=3 live from its delay slot 0x801074A4), and the corrected control flow is:

  if (entity+4 == 3) {                       // 0x8010777C lbu v1,4(s2); 0x80107784 bne v1,v0(=3),0x801077B4
      if ((FUN_80015FE8() & 3) == 0) {       // 0x8010778C jal; 0x80107794 andi v0,v0,0x3; 0x80107798 bne -> 0x801077B0
          if (entity+0x16B != 0) goto CORPSE;// 0x801077A0 lb v0,363(s2); 0x801077A8 bne -> 0x801077DC
      }
      entity+0x156 = 10;                     // 0x801077B0 sh v0,342(s2)  (v0=10 from either delay slot)
  }
  if (entity+0x10C != 0) goto CORPSE;        // 0x801077B4 lh v0,268(s2); 0x801077BC bne -> 0x801077DC
  if (*(u32*)0x800CFBD8 & 0x10000000) goto CORPSE; // 0x801077C8 lw; 0x801077D0 and; 0x801077D4 beq -> crawler

  CORPSE:  entity+0x21A &= 0xFFFB; *(u32*)(entity+4) = 7;   // 0x801077DC..0x801077F0
  CRAWLER: hitbox 200/200/200/200, +0x98 = -350, +0x9E = +350;  // 0x801077F8..0x80107818
           entity+0x10E = 0x2001;                                // 0x80107820/0x80107824
           flags = (flags & 0xF3FFFFFF) | 0x04000000;            // 0x801077D8/0x801077F4/0x80107828-0x80107838
           *(u32*)(entity+4) = (FUN_80015FE8() & 1) ? 1 : 513;   // 0x80107834-0x8010784C
           entity+0x1D3 &= 0x7F;                                 // 0x80107850-0x8010785C

Required-condition summary: entity+0x10C == 0 and (0x800CFBD8 & 0x10000000) == 0 are ALWAYS required. entity+0x16B == 0 is required ONLY when (entity+4 == 3 && (rand & 3) == 0) — so with entity+4==3 a zombie whose +0x16B is nonzero still becomes a crawler with probability 3/4.

Two further corrections: (a) entity+0x16B is not the WALK gait row on this path — it is written as rand()&1 by this same function at 0x80107524 (`sb v0,363(s2)`, delay slot of `beq v0,zero,0x80107680` at 0x80107520, after `andi v0,v0,0x1` at 0x8010751C). (b) 0x800CFBD8 bit 0x10000000 must be labeled UNKNOWN — it is read-only in EMZ0.BIN (0x801002E4, 0x801067E0, 0x801077C8, 0x80108964) and no EXE store site was found that touches that bit with an immediate; describing it as a "one-crawler latch" is unsupported. Finding it needs a PCSX-Redux write watchpoint on 0x800CFBD8 (skill re15-pcsx-watchpoint) or resolving the register-mask stores at 0x8002BA70 / 0x80058DF8 / 0x80069F98.

findings.title: Q4b-supplement — the 0x10000000 latch in 0x800CFBD8 is set/cleared by two 1-byte SCD opcodes (0x70 / 0x71)
findings.meaning: Byte-search of PSX.EXE finds 0x80058DAC at table slot 0x800A7688 and 0x80058E48 at 0x800A768C, i.e. SCD opcodes (0x800A7688-0x800A74C8)/4 = 0x70 and 0x71. Both are 1-byte opcodes (they advance the script PC by 1) that operate on the SCD's bound entity *(scd+0x154). 0x70 sets that entity's state word to 1, +0x1B8 = 0x800CFBF8, +0x1C0 = 0, +0x10E = (old & 0xAFFF) | 0x400, and SETS the 0x10000000 latch. 0x71 sets state word 1540 = 0x0604 (state 4, sub 6), +0x1C0 = 146, +0x10E = (old | 0x5000) & 0xFBFF, +0x1B8 = self, +0x156 = +0x162 = -1, and CLEARS the latch (0xEFFFFFFF). CRITICAL for the port: both masks (0xAFFF, and 0x5000/0xFBFF) PRESERVE the low 6 bits, so neither opcode changes upright-vs-crawl — they only touch the upper flag bits (0x400, 0x1000, 0x4000) of +0x10E. Do not mistake these for crawl switches.
openQuestions: The 0x10000000 latch is set by opcode 0x70 and cleared by 0x71, and Finding Q4b shows it BLOCKS the crawler-getup. Its exact game-level meaning (a 'a scripted zombie owns this slot' / 'only one crawler' interlock) is INFERRED, not proven.

verdict.why:
REFUTED on three counts. The instruction decoding is accurate, but the headline mechanism claim is false-by-exclusivity, the quoted body is truncated in a way that hides mandatory writes, and the quote carries bogus resolved addresses.

=== (1) FATAL: the latch is NOT only set/cleared by opcodes 0x70/0x71 ===
I emulated lui/addiu/ori register tracking over PSX.EXE + every COMMON/BIN overlay and enumerated EVERY store whose effective address is 0x800CFBD8 (95 sites), then filtered for ones touching 0x10000000/0xEFFFFFFF. FOUR sites, not two:
  0x80058df8 (op 0x70, SET)  0x80058e88 (op 0x71, CLEAR)  — the claimed pair
  0x8005d794 (SET)           0x8005d7fc (CLEAR)           — MISSED ENTIRELY
The missed pair, verbatim:
  8005d774: andi v0,v0,0x400            ; v0 = entity+0x10E & 0x400
  8005d778: beq  v0,zero,0x8005d7ac
  8005d77c: ori  v0,v1,0x5000           ; DELAY SLOT - always executes
  8005d780: lui  a0,0x800d
  8005d784: addiu a0,a0,-1064           ; 0x800cfbd8
  8005d788: lw   v0,0(a0)
  8005d78c: lui  v1,0x1000
  8005d790: or   v0,v0,v1
  8005d794: sw   v0,0(a0)               ; <<< SETS 0x10000000
  8005d7a0: andi v0,v0,0xefff
  ...
  8005d7c0: addiu v0,zero,65
  8005d7c4: beq  v1,v0,0x8005d7e4
  8005d7c8: addiu v0,zero,67            ; DELAY SLOT
  8005d7cc: beq  v1,v0,0x8005d7e4
  8005d7d0: addiu v0,zero,69            ; DELAY SLOT
  8005d7d4: beq  v1,v0,0x8005d7e4
  8005d7d8: addiu v0,zero,79            ; DELAY SLOT
  8005d7dc: bne  v1,v0,0x8005d800
  8005d7e4: lui  a0,0xefff
  8005d7ec: addiu v1,v1,-1064           ; 0x800cfbd8
  8005d7f0: lw   v0,0(v1)
  8005d7f4: ori  a0,a0,0xffff
  8005d7f8: and  v0,v0,a0
  8005d7fc: sw   v0,0(v1)               ; <<< CLEARS 0x10000000
This is NOT an SCD opcode. I dumped all 256 slots of 0x800A74C8: no entry lands in 0x8005d000-0x8005e000. It is the state-0 handler of a CHARACTER state table:
  800a83b8 -> 0x8005d3cc   (function start; preceded by jr ra/nop @0x8005d3c4/c8, prologue `addiu sp,sp,-320` @0x8005d3cc)
dispatched by
  8005d018: lbu v0,4(s0)
  8005d024: sll v0,v0,2
  8005d030: lw  v0,-31816(at)   ; 0x800a83b8 + state*4
  8005d038: jalr v0
  8005d03c: addu a0,s0,zero     ; DELAY SLOT
That table has the SAME shape as the zombie's 0x8010C830 — slot[4] is literally the same 0x80065C88, slots[5][6] NULL. So the latch is re-derived every tick from the entity's own +0x10E bit 0x400 (the exact bit 0x70 sets and 0x71 clears), independently of the script. A port that implements only the two opcodes will diverge.

=== (2) The 0x70 quote is truncated and its stated effect is incomplete ===
The claim's block ends at 0x80058df8, but the handler runs to 0x80058e44 and unconditionally also does:
  80058dfc: lbu v1,8(a1)
  80058e00: addiu v0,zero,200
  80058e04: sh  v0,354(a1)      ; +0x162 = 200   -- NOT in the claim
  80058e08: addiu v0,zero,69
  80058e0c: beq v1,v0,0x80058e20
  80058e10: sh  a0,342(a1)      ; DELAY SLOT, ALWAYS RUNS: +0x156 = [0x800d4b84]  -- NOT in the claim
  80058e14: addiu v0,zero,79
  80058e18: bne v1,v0,0x80058e30
  80058e20: lhu v0,540(a1)
  80058e28: andi v0,v0,0xdfff
  80058e2c: sh  v0,540(a1)      ; +0x21C &= 0xDFFF when +0x8 in {69,79}  -- NOT in the claim
"ITS MEANING" presents 0x70's effect as a closed list (state=1, +0x1B8, +0x1C0, +0x10E, latch) under STATUS=PROVEN. It is not closed. Also, "both are 1-byte opcodes (they advance the script PC by 1)" is asserted with NO quoted instruction — the PC advance lives at 0x80058e30-0x80058e3c and 0x80058e98-0x80058ea4, outside both quoted blocks. (It happens to be true; I verified it, and contrasted it with neighbouring opcode 0x73 @0x80058ef8 which does `addiu v0,v0,8`.)

=== (3) The quote carries fabricated-looking resolved addresses ===
The 0x71 block annotates `lw a1,340(a0)` as 0x800d0154, `sw v0,4(a1)` as 0x800d0004, `lhu v0,270(a1)` as 0x800d010e, `sb v1,448(a1)` as 0x800d01c0, `sw a1,440(a1)` as 0x800d01b8, and `lw v0,0(v1)` as 0x800d0000. None of those addresses exist. I reproduced them exactly by running `dis 0x80058dac 45`: the tool's register tracker carries `lui a0,0x800d` @0x80058de8 across the function boundary into the next function. Starting at 0x80058e40 they all vanish. a1 is a POINTER loaded from scd+0x154 (writers: 0x80055968/0x80055978/0x80055990/0x800559c4 store 0x800CFE14 / 0x800CFE18 / 0x800CFE1C[] there), so it is never 0x800d0000. Worse, the claim's own quote annotates `lw v0,0(v1)` @0x80058e7c as 0x800d0000 while its prose correctly says the latch is 0x800CFBD8 — the quote contradicts the conclusion it is offered as evidence for.

    80053f78: sll v0,v0,2
    80053f7c: lui at,0x800a
    80053f80: addu at,at,v0
    80053f84: lw  v0,29896(at)      ; 0x800a74c8 + op*4
    80053f8c: jalr v0

CORRECTED STATEMENT OF THE MECHANISM (what the port must implement):
The per-entity flag +0x10E bit 0x400 is the AUTHORITATIVE state; the global 0x10000000 bit of 0x800CFBD8 is a mirror of it that has TWO maintainers:

findings.title: Q4c — Third runtime path: a scripted, one-shot crawl conversion in ACTIVE upright sub_state_1 = 11
findings.meaning: A third, entirely different crawl entry. Gates, in order: the bearing/approach helper 0x80015614 (player X @0x800CFC30, player Z @0x800CFC38, tolerance 256) must return 0 in its low halfword; entity+0x1F0 (distance to player) < 0x708 = 1800; the global byte @0x800CFDCB must NOT have bit 0x80 set (a one-shot latch); and entity+0x106 must equal the global byte @0x800CFCFE. Then it sets the state word to 257 = 0x0101 (state 1 ACTIVE, sub_state_1 = 1 -> the SHARED handler 0x801025E4/0x801025EC), rewrites +0x10E as (old & 0xFFC0) | 1 — clearing exactly the 6-bit variant field and writing 1 = CRAWL while PRESERVING all upper flag bits — and finally sets the 0x80 latch bit in 0x800CFDCB so it can never fire again. Note the delay slot at 0x80104584 (`addiu v1,zero,257`) executes even when the branch is taken. Two sibling gates with the identical +0x106 == @0x800CFCFE + 0x800CFDCB&0x80 pattern exist at 0x80102F60 (crawl decision[0]) and 0x80103AFC (crawl decision[2]) but those set the state word to 257 WITHOUT touching +0x10E, so they are the crawl-side counterparts, not conversions.
openQuestions: entity+0x106 vs @0x800CFCFE: +0x106 is computed at 0x80036974 by a signed magic-number division (magic 0x91A2B3C5 @0x80036934/0x80036938, shift 10 @0x8003696C) whose divisor works out to ~1800, from a value returned by 0x8004FBA0(entity+0x84, 450, 16384). @0x800CFCFE is byte +11 of the global record *(0x800CE550), written at 0x80026D24 in the same block that publishes player X/Z. A floor/height-cell index is the natural reading, but I have NOT proven it — mark UNKNOWN until the divisor and 0x8004FBA0 are decoded.
What puts an upright zombie into sub_state_1 = 11 in the first place. My scan of state-word writes found 0x0B01 written at 0x80105AD4 and 0x80108228, both outside the ACTIVE root — not traced.

verdict.why:
The disassembly is accurate — I independently reproduced every quoted instruction and byte — but the MEANING is wrong on a load-bearing point, and the gate list is incomplete.

REFUTATION 1 (fatal): "finally sets the 0x80 latch bit in 0x800CFDCB so it can never fire again" is contradicted by literal instructions. The bit is explicitly CLEARED in two places, both keyed on the reserving entity (`lw v0,-596(v0)` = 0x800CFDAC):
  HURT — state table [2] = 0x80104F40 (prologue `80104f40: addiu sp,sp,-48` verified):
    80104f7c: lw v0,-596(v0)      0x800cfdac
    80104f84: bne v0,s1,0x80104fe0
    80104f94: lbu v0,-565(v0)     0x800cfdcb
    80104fa0: andi v0,v0,0x7f     <-- CLEARS bit 0x80
    80104fac: sb v0,-565(at)      0x800cfdcb
  DEATH — state table [3] = 0x80108250:
    801082c4: lw v0,-596(v0)      0x800cfdac
    801082cc: bne v0,s0,0x80108328
    801082dc: lbu v0,-565(v0)     0x800cfdcb
    801082e8: andi v0,v0,0x7f     <-- CLEARS bit 0x80
    801082f4: sb v0,-565(at)      0x800cfdcb
A full scan of EMZ0.BIN + PSX.EXE for lui-based accesses to 0x800CFDCB finds exactly 5 genuine stores: three OR-sets (0x80102FC0, 0x80103B2C, 0x801045B0 — all `ori v0,v0,0x80`) and these two AND-clears. So 0x800CFDCB bit 0x80 is a re-armable, GLOBAL, cross-path reservation flag released on hurt/death — not a permanent one-shot. A port implementing "can never fire again" diverges the moment the holder is shot.

REFUTATION 2: the enumerated "Gates, in order" omits a gate that sits on the path. Between the phase-1 body and the flip block:
    8010450c: lbu v0,333(s0)          ; entity+0x14D
    80104514: sltiu v0,v0,0x12
    80104518: bne v0,zero,0x801045bc  ; delay slot 8010451c: addu a0,s0,zero
    (raw bytes 8010450c: 4d 01 02 92 | 00 00 00 00 | 12 00 42 2c | 28 00 40 14)

REFUTATION 3 (labeling): "player X @0x800CFC30, player Z @0x800CFC38" is INFERRED, not PROVEN. The only genuine writer is EXE 80026ccc: `sw v0,-976(at)` / 80026d0c: `sw v0,-968(at)`, sourced from `lhu v0,0(a1)` / `lhu v0,4(a1)` of an unidentified struct a1; 0x800CFCFE likewise from `80026d24: sb v1,-770(at)` fed by `lbu v1,11(a1)`. WHAT I DID CONFIRM (so it can be reused): decision[11]=0x80104394 (`jr ra`/`nop`) and executor[11]=0x8010439C, both read out of tables 0x8010C88C/0x8010C8CC. verdict.correction:
Corrected statement of the finding:

ACTIVE upright sub_state_1 = 11, sub_state_2 = 1 (executor 0x8010439C; decision 0x80104394 is a bare `jr ra`) contains an upright->crawl conversion. It runs only when FIVE conditions hold, in this order:
  1. entity+0x14D >= 0x12 (18)                     @8010450c/80104514/80104518  [meaning of +0x14D UNKNOWN]
  2. helper 0x80015614(entity, @0x800CFC30, @0x800CFC38, tol=256) returns 0 in its low halfword — i.e. entity facing is within +/-256/4096 of the bearing to that target   @80104530-8010453c
  3. entity+0x1F0 (distance to player) < 0x708 = 1800   @80104544/8010454c
  4. global 0x800CFDCB & 0x80 == 0                     @8010455c/80104564
  5. entity+0x106 == global byte 0x800CFCFE            @80104570-80104580
Then it writes state word +0x4 = 257 = 0x0101 (state 1 ACTIVE, sub_state_1 = 1, and note the `sw` also zeroes +0x6 and +0x7) @8010458c, rewrites +0x10E = (old & 0xFFC0) | 1 @80104588-80104598 — clearing exactly the 6-bit variant field (`8010115c: andi v0,v0,0x3f`) and selecting 0x8010C854[1] = 0x80101210 CRAWL while preserving the upper flag bits — so the next tick lands in crawl-table entry [1] = 0x801025E4 / 0x801025EC (shared with upright entry [3]). Finally it sets 0x800CFDCB |= 0x80 @801045a8/801045b0.

Bit 0x80 of 0x800CFDCB is NOT a permanent one-shot. It is a GLOBAL, cross-path reservation flag: set by exactly three sites (0x80102FC0 crawl decision[0], 0x80103B2C crawl decision[2], 0x801045B0 this conversion) and CLEARED by `andi v0,v0,0x7f` in HURT 0x80104FA0/0x80104FAC and DEATH 0x801082E8/0x801082F4, each gated on 0x800CFDAC == the entity. Both clears also do `andi v1,v1,0xed` on 0x800CFDB8. Consequence for the port: after the holding zombie is hurt or killed the flag re-arms and any of the three gates can fire again — model it as a released reservation, not as "never again".

Still UNKNOWN, do not invent: the identity of 0x800CFC30/0x800CFC38 (written at EXE 0x80026CCC/0x80026D0C from `lhu 0(a1)` / `lhu 4(a1)` of an unidentified struct — plausibly the player, since the entity's own X/Z live at +0x38/+0x40 and 0x800CFC30-0x38 = 0x800CFBF8 gives +0x40 = 0x800CFC38, but that is INFERRED); the identity of 0x800CFCFE (EXE 0x80026D24 from `lbu v1,11(a1)`); the identity of 0x800CFDAC and 0x800CFBFC (== 5 gate at 0x80104F6C); and the meaning of entity+0x14D and +0x21A. Resolving these needs the caller of the EXE function containing 0x80026CCC (to identify a1) and a writer search for 0x800CFDAC.

findings.meaning: PROVEN structure: state 8 is a two-level machine — the root selects one of 11 handlers by sub_state_1 (+0x5), and each handler runs its own phase machine on +0x6 through a secondary table located in a DATA BLOCK at the very start of the overlay (0x8010016C, 0x80100184, 0x8010019C, 0x801001CC/0x801001DC, 0x80100204, 0x8010022C — the overlay's first ~0x260 bytes are data, which is also why INIT does lwl/lwr copies from 0x80100004). Handlers 5/6, 7/8 and 9/10 are shared pairs. Every handler resolves a PARTNER entity: `lh v0,474(s0)` reads entity+0x1DA, scales by 4 and indexes the entity pointer array based at 0x800CFE14 (the object list iterated by the EXE tick loop starts one slot later, at 0x800CFE18 — see 0x8004A6F8). The zombie then turns toward the partner's +0x38/+0x40 (X/Z) with helper 0x80015558, and at 0x80109FB0-0x80109FF0 it TAKES OVER the partner: writes the partner's state word to 8196 = 0x2004, sets partner+0x1B4 to a back-pointer to the zombie, copies its own +0x188/+0x18C into the partner, and ORs 0x1000 into both entities' flag words. Substates 5..10 then read +0x1B4 back out and puppeteer the partner (sb ...,6(s1) / sw ...,332(s1) / sh ...,118(s1) / sw ...,4(s1)), with blood/effect calls at 0x8010B548-0x8010B5C4 (0x800395B8, 0x80039514, 0x8003947C) and sound calls 0x8005BA28 / 0x8005BD6C. Since +0x1DA is settable ONLY by SCD Member_set member 26 and +0x4 only by member 2, state 8 is entirely script-initiated. RE1.5 has no [8] slot at all, so this whole paired-actor machine is RE2-exclusive and has no port counterpart.
openQuestions: What the state IS in game terms. The evidence (a script-named partner entity, the zombie seizing the partner's state/animation pointers, a long 11-substate sequence with blood effects) is consistent with a scripted zombie-feeding/mauling set-piece, but I did not find a damage call or a string that names it. I am NOT asserting a name.

Substates 9/10 (0x8010B464) build a 2-byte local table {13,15} at sp+24/25 and index it with `lbu v0,5(s2)` (0x8010B4C4) — with +0x5 == 9 or 10 that reads past the pair into saved registers. Either those two table slots are dead, or +0x5 is rewritten before entry. UNRESOLVED — this needs a live savestate to settle, and a port must not blindly reproduce the OOB read.

Whether the partner is the player (array index 0) or an NPC: the object list the EXE ticks starts at 0x800CFE18 = index 1, so index 0 is a special slot, but I did not find the writer of *(0x800CFE14) and therefore cannot claim it is the player.
